transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Lina Torres (AE), Marcus Lee (SE) — Redwood; Priya Banerjee, Carlos Mendes, Hannah Ortiz — Aurelia Financial

Summary (auto): Quick check: access gating, first-day latency, and next steps for benching and KMS. Some audio dropouts and mislabels.

[00:00] Lina Torres: hey everyone, um thanks for joining, we'll just do a quick 45 minute sync — call it week four of the POC. 
[00:12] Priya Banerjee: yeah thanks lina, we've got Carlos and Hannah on; we've got a few infra people queued to look at the secrets issue. 
[00:24] Marcus Lee: great, I'll kick off with the latency numbers we saw in staging this morning, and then we can go through access and the KMS thing. 
[00:36] Carlos Mendes: quick note — we had a firewall rule that blocked the gateway egress earlier, fixed that at 9:10, so some of the initial tests errored out. 
[00:49] Hannah Ortiz: and from product side we want to confirm the success criteria: 99th p95? sorry p95 and p99 targets? I mean p95 under 180ms is our goal. 
[00:59] Lina Torres: right, p95 under 180ms is what we discussed, and we'll show the bench results. 
[01:10] Marcus Lee: ok so real quick numbers, this is from the short 24 hour snapshot — median was 110ms, p95 sits at 220ms, p99 around 410ms. note that the early tests that failed because of egress made the p99 spike — so I'm flagging that. 
[01:32] Priya Banerjee: 410ms... that's higher than we hoped, was that with quantization enabled? 
[01:41] Marcus Lee: no, that run was default FP16 on our shared hosted profile; we didn't apply the quant profile yet. once we apply int8 calibrations we usually see token latency drop — but we also saw cold-start KV cache misses, so a warming strategy would help. 
[02:02] Carlos Mendes: can you explain the KV cache miss? we saw some 'cache not found' logs. is that per-instance cache or shared? 
[02:12] Marcus Lee: good question — Redwood's runtime keeps per-worker KV cache and we have prefix caching. When new instances spun up due to burst the cache wasn't warmed, so initial requests hit model compute. For your workload with short multi-turns we recommend persistent prefix cache and a small prefill ramp. 
[02:36] Speaker 4 (QA): um can the prefill be done during low-traffic windows automatically? 
[02:43] Marcus Lee: yes, you can run background prefill; we also have a batch pre-warm mechanism in our dedicated offering. We'll share a script. 
[02:54] Priya Banerjee: on the KMS front we hit an error when trying to decrypt tokens from staging — the service account doesn't have decrypt rights per the audit. Carlos, can you confirm the IAM role? 
[03:07] Carlos Mendes: yeah that was my bad, I left the role scoped to project-level without Cloud KMS Decrypt. I'll update and retry. 
[03:14] Lina Torres: ok thanks — that ties to the security doc I'll send. We'll include the KMS playbook and the minimal IAM perms. 
[03:23] Priya Banerjee: also curious about observability — where will traces land and how do we correlate request ids? 
[03:32] Marcus Lee: we push traces to your datadog endpoint or you can use the console. The request-id is included in the token returned and in the log line. There may be some parsing quirks right now, we've seen slight field name mismatches. 
[03:48] Hannah Ortiz: is there a guide for mapping our internal request ids to the Redwood trace ids? 
[03:54] Lina Torres: yes, Marcus will drop a snippet in the shared doc. 
[04:00] Marcus Lee: action item: I'll run a 1k request bench using your sample payloads — two runs, default FP16 and int8 quant, capture GPU metrics and traces. 
[04:13] Priya Banerjee: perfect — when do you think you'll have that? 
[04:18] Marcus Lee: aiming by Monday the 20th, so due 2026-07-20, unless we find infra blockers. 
[04:25] Carlos Mendes: once Marcus posts traces we'll correlate with our logs. also I need Lina to send the SOC2 artifact and the KMS instructions. 
[04:33] Lina Torres: yep I'll send the security pack and the KMS runbook by Friday 2026-07-18. 
[04:41] Hannah Ortiz: re: cost, any quick notes on cost impact of int8 quant vs FP16? we need to know ballpark for forecast. 
[04:50] Marcus Lee: at inference layer int8 reduces GPU cycles and memory, so you get a drop in per-token cost and improvements in throughput; we'll include a cost delta in the bench report but roughly 20-30% in our typical workloads — depends on batch and seq length. 
[05:07] Priya Banerjee: can we also request a burst plan? sometimes production-like loads spike in the morning. 
[05:13] Lina Torres: yes we can propose a dedicated burst plan; I'll include a preliminary cost estimate in the doc. 
[05:20] Carlos Mendes: one more infra question — do you support static IPs for egress? our firewall rules prefer static allow list. 
[05:28] Marcus Lee: hosted endpoints currently support a small set of egress ranges; for static single-IP you'll want Dedicated or the Private deployment with NAT. I'll outline options in the write-up. 
[05:41] Speaker 4 (QA): small audio blip...
[05:45] Priya Banerjee: we also want to confirm data retention defaults — we are regulated and need 30 day logs, not longer. 
[05:53] Lina Torres: Redwood defaults are 90 days, but for enterprise we can configure retention windows — we'll include retention options in the security pack. 
[06:06] Marcus Lee: ok next, quick note on the bench plan — two runs with 1k requests each, mix of single-turn (60%) and 3-turn conversation (40%), payloads from your sample set. We'll attach the spreadsheet with token counts and cost calc. 
[06:23] Priya Banerjee: do you need any more sample data from us? 
[06:27] Marcus Lee: just the service account for benching and your list of gateway IPs to whitelist; and if you want us to simulate your auth headers we can. 
[06:36] Carlos Mendes: sending the svc-account and ip list today. 
[06:40] Hannah Ortiz: timeline check — if benches look good, when can we run canary traffic? 
[06:44] Lina Torres: we proposed Tuesday 2026-07-21 for canary 10% traffic. If benches pass and KMS is validated, that remains doable. 
[06:54] Priya Banerjee: ok, can we have a short dry-run before canary? like a smoke test? 
[06:59] Marcus Lee: yes, we can do a smoke test the day before. 
[07:04] Speaker 4 (QA): quick note — we saw some transcription mismatches in the console; may be metadata mapping issue. 
[07:10] Marcus Lee: noted, we'll include mapping tips. 
[07:16] Lina Torres: any other blockers? 
[07:20] Priya Banerjee: only KMS and the initial firewall fix — both in progress. 
[07:25] Carlos Mendes: will update once IAM perms fixed. 
[07:28] Lina Torres: great. recap: Marcus runs bench and uploads traces by 2026-07-20; Lina sends SOC2/KMS doc by 2026-07-18; customer provides svc-account and IP list by 2026-07-19; schedule smoke on 2026-07-20 and canary on 2026-07-21. 
[07:48] Hannah Ortiz: thanks all. 
[07:50] Lina Torres: thanks everyone, end.

Auto notes: occasional dropped words and mis-attributed speakers (Speaker 4). References to shared artifacts: shared sheet link (internal), security doc (will be sent), bench spreadsheet.
